hints: Focus on what standard enthalpy change of reaction really means, the heat change for the molar amounts exactly as written in the balanced equation.
Look closely at the coefficients in this equation, 1 mole of XeF6, 3 moles of water, 1 mole of XeO3 and 6 moles of HF.
Ask yourself which statement matches those exact reacting amounts, with all substances in their standard states.
walkthrough:
**Recall the definition of standard enthalpy change of reaction**

Standard enthalpy change of reaction, $\Delta H_r^\ominus$, is the enthalpy change when the amounts of reactants and products react and form exactly as shown by the balanced equation, with everything in standard states.

Definition:
$$\Delta H_r^\ominus = \text{enthalpy change for molar quantities as per balanced equation}$$

**Read the molar quantities in this equation**

Look at the numbers in front of each formula. They tell you the exact recipe for one enthalpy change.

Given equation:
$$\text{XeF}_6 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{XeO}_3 + 6\text{HF}$$
This means 1 mol $\text{XeF}_6$ reacts with 3 mol $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ to make 1 mol $\text{XeO}_3$ and 6 mol $\text{HF}$.

**Match the statement to the recipe**

We cannot scale down to 1 mole total or 1 mole of water, because that would change the equation. The only statement that keeps the full recipe is the one describing 6 moles of $\text{HF}$ being produced, which automatically means 1 mole of $\text{XeF}_6$, 3 moles of water and 1 mole of $\text{XeO}_3$ are involved too.

options.A: Incorrect. One mole of products in total would be only a fraction of this reaction, since the equation makes 1 + 6 = 7 moles of products. Standard enthalpy change of reaction uses the full amounts as written, not scaled to one mole total.
options.B: Incorrect. One mole of reactants in total would also be a scaled down fraction, since the equation uses 1 + 3 = 4 moles of reactants. This confuses standard enthalpy of reaction with a per mole total idea.
options.C: Incorrect. The equation shows 3 moles of water reacting, not 1 mole. The enthalpy change for 1 mole of water would be only one third of the standard enthalpy change of reaction for the equation as written.
options.D: Correct. The equation produces exactly 6 moles of HF when 1 mole of XeF6 reacts with 3 moles of water to give 1 mole of XeO3. Stating 6 moles of HF are produced describes the full reaction exactly as written, so it correctly defines the standard enthalpy change of reaction.
